title: Free Big Five personality test (IPIP 50 questions) — cv.cm
description: Take the free Big Five (OCEAN) personality test with the public-domain IPIP 50-item questionnaire. See your openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness and neuroticism scores. No sign-up.
lede: Measure the five traits psychologists use most: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism. 50 short statements, results as five scores out of 100.
about: The Big Five (also called the Five-Factor Model or OCEAN) is the best-researched model of personality. Instead of putting you in a box, it places you on five independent scales, so everyone gets a unique profile.

This test uses the 50-item Big-Five Factor Markers from the International Personality Item Pool (IPIP), developed by Lewis Goldberg and placed in the public domain. Scores here are compared to the scale range, not to a population sample, so 50 means the middle of the scale.

faq.a: Openness to experience, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness and Neuroticism, the five broad traits in the model.
No. Each end of a trait has strengths. Low extraversion goes with focus and calm; low agreeableness with candor and independence.

faq.q: Is the Big Five more scientific than MBTI?
faq.a: Most personality researchers prefer the Big Five: its traits are measured as continuous scores and predict outcomes like job performance and wellbeing in many studies.

faq.q: Where do the questions come from?
faq.a: From the IPIP 50-item Big-Five Factor Markers by Lewis Goldberg, a public-domain questionnaire used widely in research.

items: Am the life of the party.
Am relaxed most of the time.
Am not interested in abstract ideas.
Am not interested in other people's problems.
Often forget to put things back in their proper place.
Do not have a good imagination.
Talk to a lot of different people at parties.
Am not really interested in others.
Don't like to draw attention to myself.
Don't mind being the center of attention.

O.low: You prefer the familiar and the practical. You like proven ways of doing things and concrete facts over abstract speculation.
O.mid: You balance curiosity with practicality: open to new ideas when they are useful, comfortable with routine when it works.
O.high: You are curious, imaginative and drawn to ideas, art and new experiences. You enjoy abstract thinking and variety.

C.low: You are flexible and spontaneous, and you dislike rigid plans. Deadlines and tidiness may take conscious effort.
C.mid: You are organized when it matters and relaxed when it doesn't. You can plan, but you don't need everything scheduled.
C.high: You are organized, dependable and goal-driven. You plan ahead, pay attention to details, and follow through.

E.low: You are reserved and recharge alone or with a few close people. You think before you speak and enjoy quiet focus.
E.mid: You are an ambivert: sociable in the right setting, but you also value time to yourself.
E.high: You are outgoing, talkative and energized by people. You enjoy attention, groups and a lively pace.

A.low: You are frank, skeptical and competitive. You say what you think and don't mind disagreement.
A.mid: You are generally cooperative but can stand your ground. You weigh others' needs against your own.
A.high: You are warm, trusting and helpful. You care about harmony and other people's feelings.

N.low: You are emotionally steady and calm under pressure. Setbacks rarely shake you for long.
N.mid: You feel stress and worry at normal levels and usually recover from them in a reasonable time.
N.high: You feel emotions intensely and can be prone to worry, stress or low moods. Regular rest, exercise and talking things through help.
